questions.prompt: You run `bash deploy.sh` in your terminal. What does the `#!/bin/sh` line do?

options.a: forces the script to run under sh anyway
options.b: nothing — it's a comment; the shebang only picks the interpreter when the file itself is exec'd (./deploy.sh)
options.c: makes bash switch into POSIX mode

questions.prompt: Name one bash-only construct from deploy.sh that dash rejects.

options.a: Debian's small, fast, POSIX-compliant sh — what /bin/sh points to on Debian/Ubuntu
options.c: an obsolete shell that bash replaced
